info.title: OLF2.0 Machine to Machine Service API
info.description: **Access** For integration with the environment an explicit request for production client credentials needs to be made to support@epo.org. A B2B account will be created for you, and we will provide you with the client id and secret for your account. When you have the B2B account details, your OLF2.0 organisation administrator needs to add the B2B user as a member to your organisation. To do so, in OLF2.0 the organisation administrator needs to: - Open the "Administration" area, and select the "Access rights / permissions" subtab - Select "Add" on the top right of the user table - Enter the full user name of the B2B account (first name and last name) as provided by the EPO - Enter the EPO account number as provided by the EPO - Select "Save" If the name and EPO account number entered match those provided to you by the EPO, the B2B user will be added to your organisation and listed in the user table below. - Select the newly added B2B user from the table - Select "Manage rights / permissions" - Select the EP forms which you intend to be importing with the B2B API, and ensure that the you grant at least "Draft" rights (if you intend to be performing submissions via the B2B API, "Send" rights are also necessary) - For the B2B user to be functional in production, make sure that the "Access to Online Filing 2.0" right is also granted (access to demo is granted by default for all users of an organisation) **Authentication** In order to use the API please follow OAuth 2.0 standard with the provided client credentials (client_id and Secret). As such, your IP Management System should first make a call to the EPO's authentication service using the provided credentials to obtain an access token. The obtained bearer access token as well as organisation id can then be used in the second call to one of the various endpoints of the OLF2.0 "Machine to Machine" service. **Endpoint description** The following endpoints are provided: 1. Import Supports the importing of an EP packages in folders. The full folder path needs to be provided from the root folder (the "Submissions" page in OLF2.0). E.g. /folder1/folder2/ will import the package to "folder2" which is inside "folder1". Upon a successful import, the validation log is returned which lists the critical errors (i.e. red validation messages in OLF2.0) and warnings (i.e. yellow validation messages in OLF2.0) Non-signed packages are imported in the "Draft" status. Signed packages are imported in the "Ready to Send" status, only if there are no critical validation errors. 2. Submissions Returns a list of submissions of the organisation in chronological order. Supports filtering by creation date (ranged), folder path, and submission status. Can be paginated using the offset and limit parameters. 3. Delete Supports the deletion of a package. It is only possible to delete packages imported by the B2B API user and which are not in the "Submitted" status 4. Export Supports the export of the binary (zip) of a package. If octet-stream is specified as the format parameter, the response is provided as a byte stream. If no format parameter is specified, the response is provided as a zip file with binary data. 5. Status Returns the status of a submission package, as it appears in OLF2.0 6. Submit Supports the submission of a package. The package needs to be in status "Ready to Send" 7. Package files Returns a list of the the files (filenames) included in a submission package 8. Download Supports the download of an individual file from a package 9. ImportPCT Supports the import of International Applications (PCT applications) into folders. The full folder path needs to be provided from the root folder (the "Submissions" page in OLF2.0). E.g. /folder1/folder2/ will import the package to "folder2" which is inside "folder1". Upon a successful import, the validation log is returned which lists the warnings and critical errors as these are provided by ePCT. The structure of the IA package needs to conform to the requirements/structure of packages as these are supported by WIPO's ePCT. 10. Folders Returns a list of top level folders of the organisation. **For testing purposes and the use of this swagger page** Please use the URL of the EPO's authentication service [https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server](https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) with the provided clientId and secret and ask for mailboxapi scope. Below you can find a command to create the bearer access_token using *curl* and the related sample output ``` curl --location 'https://login.epo.org/oauth2/aus6hh2ns9ORf2PD3417/v1/token' --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' --data-urlencode 'client_id={CLIENT_ID}' --data-urlencode 'client_secret={SECRET}' --data-urlencode 'scope=mailboxapi' ``` ***Sample Output*** ``` { "access_token": "abc1234asdf9823...", "expires_in": 18000, "scope": "mailboxapi", "token_type": "Bearer" } ``` The value of the property access_token can be pasted in the bearerAuth input field shown when clicking on the "Authorize" button in this page. Once Authorised, endpoints can be triggered through this page. **Support** If you need help or would like to provide feedback, please send an email to our support desk: support@epo.org **ChangeLog** v2.2 - Added endpoint to return the list of files included within a submission package - Added endpoint to download a single file included in a submission package v2.3 - Added endpoint to support the import of International Applications (PCT applications) v2.4 - Added endpoint to list folders - Added filtering parameters to the submissions endpoint **Standards** The API is implementing ST90 standards except the following points: - The API does not support RSG[21-27] in regards to providing XML representation of the resource - The API does not support RSG[100] in regards to specifying request timeout by the client - The API does not support RSG[101-104,107] in regards to supporting caching of the resource - The API does not support RSG[107] in regards to providing sending large files in chunks

tags.name: B2B API
tags.description: B2B endpoints for managing patent submissions

put.description: Moves a submission to the specified folder. The target folder must exist. Use 'List folders' endpoint to see available folders.

post.description: Initiates the submission process by sending the submission to the EPO mediation server. The submission must be in READY_TO_SEND status before it can be submitted. After successful submission, the status changes to SUBMITTED.

400.description: Submission is not in a valid state for sending

post.description: Imports a PCT (Patent Cooperation Treaty) draft submission package. The uploaded file must be a valid ZIP archive in the PCT submission format. Returns a UUID that uniquely identifies the imported submission. Optionally specify a folder path to organize the imported draft.

400.description: Invalid PCT package format or corrupted ZIP file

post.description: Imports a draft submission package into the system. The uploaded file must be a valid ZIP archive in the EPO submission format. Returns a UUID that uniquely identifies the imported submission. Optionally specify a folder path to organize the imported draft.

400.description: Invalid package format or corrupted ZIP file

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of submissions for the authenticated user's organisation. Supports filtering by creation date range, folder path, and submission status. 

**Pagination:** Use 'limit' and 'offset' parameters. Default: limit=10, offset=0.

**Sorting:** Use 'order' parameter with value 'asc' or 'desc' (by creation date). Default: asc.

**Status filter:** Use 'submissionStatus' to filter by one or more statuses. Multiple statuses can be provided as comma-separated values. The status names returned in the response match the filter values exactly. 

Available statuses: DRAFT, READY_TO_SIGN, READY_TO_SEND, SUBMITTED, REVISED, INACTIVE, READY_TO_SEND_PROCESSING_SUBMISSION, READY_TO_SEND_RETRY_NEEDED, SUBMITTED_SUBMISSION_CREATED, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_OLF_PROCESSING, SUBMITTED_PROCESSING_RECEIPT, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_RECEIPT_RETRIEVAL, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_SUBMISSION, SUBMITTED_PROCESSING_RECEIPT_PENDING_FOR_AUTOMATIC_RETRY, SUBMITTED_RETRY_PROCESSING_RECEIPT, PCT_CREATED.

**Examples:**
- List drafts: `?submissionStatus=DRAFT`
- List drafts and submitted: `?submissionStatus=DRAFT,SUBMITTED`
- Paginated with date filter: `?limit=20&offset=0&createdDateFrom=2025-01-01&createdDateTo=2025-12-31`
- Combined filters: `?submissionStatus=READY_TO_SEND&order=desc&limit=50`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of submissions to return. Must be a positive integer.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of submissions to skip (for pagination). Must be a non-negative integer.

parameters.name: createdDateFrom
parameters.description: Filter by creation date (from), inclusive. Format: yyyy-MM-dd

parameters.name: createdDateTo
parameters.description: Filter by creation date (to), inclusive. Format: yyyy-MM-dd

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort order by creation date. Allowed values: 'asc', 'desc'. Default: asc

parameters.name: submissionStatus
parameters.description: Filter by submission status. Comma-separated for multiple values. Available: DRAFT, READY_TO_SIGN, READY_TO_SEND, SUBMITTED, REVISED, INACTIVE, READY_TO_SEND_PROCESSING_SUBMISSION, READY_TO_SEND_RETRY_NEEDED, SUBMITTED_SUBMISSION_CREATED, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_OLF_PROCESSING, SUBMITTED_PROCESSING_RECEIPT, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_RECEIPT_RETRIEVAL, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_SUBMISSION, SUBMITTED_PROCESSING_RECEIPT_PENDING_FOR_AUTOMATIC_RETRY, SUBMITTED_RETRY_PROCESSING_RECEIPT, PCT_CREATED

400.description: Invalid parameter value (e.g. non-numeric limit/offset, invalid status name, invalid order)

get.description: Returns the current status of a submission. Possible statuses: DRAFT, READY_TO_SIGN, READY_TO_SEND, SUBMITTED, REVISED, INACTIVE, READY_TO_SEND_PROCESSING_SUBMISSION, READY_TO_SEND_RETRY_NEEDED, SUBMITTED_SUBMISSION_CREATED, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_OLF_PROCESSING, SUBMITTED_PROCESSING_RECEIPT, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_RECEIPT_RETRIEVAL, SUBMITTED_ERROR_DURING_SUBMISSION, SUBMITTED_PROCESSING_RECEIPT_PENDING_FOR_AUTOMATIC_RETRY, SUBMITTED_RETRY_PROCESSING_RECEIPT, PCT_CREATED.
Returns a list of all file names contained in the submission package. Use these file names with the 'Download single package file' endpoint to download individual files.

Exports the complete submission package as a downloadable file. The submission must exist and contain all mandatory files. Returns the package as a binary stream with appropriate content-type headers.

5050.description: Mandatory file not found in the submission package

get.description: Downloads a specific file from a submission package. Use the 'List submission package files' endpoint to get available file names.

parameters.name: fileName
parameters.description: Name of the file to download

404.description: File not found in the submission package

get.description: Returns a list of all folder paths available for the authenticated user's organisation. Folder paths can be used with the 'List submissions' and 'Move submission' endpoints.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a submission and all associated files. This action cannot be undone.
